target.title: feat(onboarding): prefer strongest local model in guided detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guided onboarding auto-detects running local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio) and offers one of their models as the zero-key inference route, but it picks the FIRST tools-capable model discovery returns — effectively random for users with many pulled models. A 70B llama or a coder/vision specialist can win over an ideal small instruct model, giving a slow or poorly-suited model for the setup assistant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Onboarding's detected-candidate quality decides whether the conversational setup (system agent) works well. Small mainstream instruct families (Qwen3.x, Gemma 4, etc.) are the strongest tool-callers per current BFCL-class results; specialists (embedding/vision/rerank) and coder variants are worse choices for a setup assistant. Both plugins had the same naive pick, so the ranking lives once in the plugin SDK (`extensions/AGENTS.md`: shared helper over per-plugin copies).

- New `selectPreferredLocalModelId` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-model-shared`: deterministic family-preference ranking (gemma4 > qwen3.5 > qwen3 > gpt-oss > gemma3 > llama4 > llama3 > phi4 > mistral > deepseek), coder-variant and specialist sinking, caller-order stability. Heuristic contract, safe to retune.
- `extensions/ollama`: app-guided discovery ranks all tools-capable models instead of taking the first.
- `extensions/lmstudio`: default-model selection keeps the explicit documented default, then ranks, then falls back to first.
- `docs/cli/setup.md`: documents the preference in the setup bootstrap ladder contract.
- SDK surface budget +1 with the standard checker-workflow comment; API baseline regenerated via `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`.

## User Impact

Users with several local models get the strongest setup-assistant model picked automatically during `openclaw onboard` / `openclaw setup`; behavior with zero or one model is unchanged. No config surface changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/provider-model-shared.test.ts` — 30 passed (pairwise family order, specialist/coder sinking, size-tag vs version disambiguation, stability, empty input).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama` — 16 files, 371 passed (incl. new multi-model preference test).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/lmstudio` — 6 files, 117 passed (incl. new preference tests).
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` + `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — clean.
- Autoreview (codex, gpt-5.6-sol, branch vs origin/main): clean, no actionable findings.
- Live model bench backing the ranking order (macOS, Ollama, real system-agent prompts/parsers driven directly; 10 scenarios x 3 repeats per mode): planner-contract mode gemma4:e4b 26/30 vs qwen3.5:4b 13/30 (both ~100% valid JSON via the tolerant extractor); native tool-call mode gemma4:e4b 25/30 (median 2.7s/turn) vs qwen3.5:4b 21/30 (median 6.8s/turn). Qwen3.5 failed the approval-follow-through scenario 0/6 across both modes (wrong action or claims success without a command); with thinking enabled its latency exceeds 2min/turn. Hence gemma4 ranks first.

Related: #109228 (local-model onboarding track — Apple Foundation Models provider card).

target.title: fix(acp): keep completed run-mode sessions resumable
target.body:
Closes #106696.

## What Problem This Solves

ACP sessions spawned with `mode="run"` are intentionally closed after their first turn. A later `sessions_send` to the same completed child therefore started a fresh agent conversation or failed with missing ACP metadata instead of resuming the backend conversation. This made parent agents unable to answer questions or continue work in an existing one-shot Codex or Claude session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manager now retains completed one-shot metadata only when the agent advertises ACP session resume/load support, a stable ACP session ID has been recorded, the identity is resolved rather than provisional, and the terminal turn confirms that the session is ready to resume. A parent follow-up resumes that ID, fails closed if resume fails, and keeps OpenClaw's one-shot lifecycle while reconnecting through ACPX under a fresh process lease.

The change also distinguishes a live prompt from terminal cleanup, pins resumed one-shots to the backend that owns the resume ID, and avoids duplicate inline/task delivery. Active turns, unsupported agents, unmaterialized sessions, invalid resume targets, and transient non-session ACP errors remain handled conservatively.

## User Impact

Parents can follow up with completed ACP run-mode children without losing task context. Codex and Claude one-shots preserve their working directory and conversation state across the follow-up, while unsupported or unsafe resume states fail explicitly instead of silently starting a fresh conversation.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `7a81f299803`:

- `pnpm test:extension acpx`: 14 files, 179 tests passed
- focused ACP manager suite: 4 files, 32 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit src/acp/control-plane/manager.identity-reconcile.test.ts`: 2 tests passed on the exact head
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project agents-core src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts`: 40 tests passed on the exact head
- `pnpm tsgo:test`: passed on the exact head
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main`: passed
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed
- `pnpm check`: passed on the exact head
- `pnpm build`: passed on the exact head
- `codex review --base upstream/main`: one provisional-identity finding fixed with a regression test; exact-head re-review found no further correctness defects

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A completed ACP `mode="run"` child lost its original conversation when the parent later used `sessions_send`, causing a fresh-session response or `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` instead of a contextual follow-up.
- **Real environment tested:** A Linux system running a long-lived OpenClaw gateway from a local build with the bundled ACPX extension, using both Claude ACP and Codex ACP child sessions launched by a parent agent.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Spawned a one-shot child that returned a unique context marker, waited for the run to complete and its runtime process to be cleaned up, then sent a follow-up through `sessions_send` to the same OpenClaw ACP session key asking for the marker. Repeated the flow for Claude and Codex.
- **Evidence after fix:** The initial child output contained `CONTEXT_TOKEN=<redacted-marker>`. The later follow-up returned the same marker under the same OpenClaw ACP session key and backend transcript ID. Neither follow-up reported a fresh session or missing task context.
- **Observed result after fix:** Completed Claude and Codex one-shots resumed their original backend conversation and answered the parent follow-up with the prior context intact. An actually active one-shot was still rejected, and an invalid resume target failed closed rather than silently starting fresh.
- **What was not tested:** Windows and macOS were not exercised in the real setup. The final stale-`closed` process-lease recovery and terminal-delivery race refinements were validated with unit/integration tests, not by deliberately crashing the production gateway during those exact windows.

## AI-assisted disclosure

This PR is AI-assisted. I ran the real behavior validation and automated tests, reviewed the implementation and review findings, and understand the metadata, resume-capability, lifecycle, delivery, backend-pinning, and process-lease changes in this patch.

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI rendered a broken/garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph. This PR fixes that by using `Intl.Segmenter` to extract complete grapheme clusters.

## Summary

- **Problem**: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit), breaking on emoji/astral Unicode.
- **Solution**: New `deriveAvatarInitial` helper using `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"`. Falls back to surrogate-pair-aware extraction for browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` (Firefox 114-124).
- **What changed**:
  - `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` with feature detection + fallback (no behavior change for ASCII)
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — sidebar chip avatar uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — agent selector fallback uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts` — agent menu row initial uses helper
  - `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts` — agents overview identity editor avatar uses helper
  - `ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts` — dedicated real-Chromium E2E covering all four surfaces
- **All four call sites now share the identical `(deriveAvatarInitial(...) || "?")` empty-input fallback** for consistent behavior.
- **What did NOT change**: ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites (ASCII-only inputs); the plugin monogram in `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts` (see coordination note).

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased onto current `main` (`55a822dc687`). The upstream `app-sidebar.ts` refactor (now extending `AppSidebarMenusElement`, ~688 LOC) moved the chip-avatar fallback; the affected call site still exists and was reapplied at `app-sidebar.ts:615-617`. Import-block conflict from the refactor was resolved manually. The rebased diff against `main` is exactly the 8 files above (+319 / -7).

## The four affected surfaces

A full scan of remaining `.slice(0, 1)` avatar-initial fallback sites found all four **live** surfaces sharing the identical bug:

- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — sidebar chip avatar
- `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — agent selector dropdown fallback
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts` — agent menu row initial
- `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts` — agents overview identity editor avatar

All now route through `deriveAvatarInitial` and are covered by the E2E below.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With `Intl.Segmenter`** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): complete grapheme clusters preserved (emoji, joined emoji, flags, skin-tone).
- **Without `Intl.Segmenter`** (Firefox 114-124): first complete code point extracted (surrogate-pair-aware), no garbled surrogate half.

## Evidence

**Real browser proof** (Playwright real Chromium, mocked Gateway), all four avatar surfaces, captured on the rebased `main`:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \
    ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts

✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the sidebar chip and agent menu row
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agent selector dropdown
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agents overview identity editor
3 passed
```

Each surface's rendered avatar text is asserted `.toBe("🚀")` — the intact grapheme cluster, not a dangling surrogate half — read from the real browser DOM. Full-page screenshots captured locally (NOT committed, per repo visual-proof policy): `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/avatar-initial-emoji/{01-sidebar-chip-emoji,02-agent-selector-emoji,03-agents-overview-emoji}.png`.

**Unit + component tests**:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
20 passed
```

Helper unit tests cover both the `Intl.Segmenter` path and the stubbed-`undefined` fallback path (emoji, ZWJ family, flags, skin-tone, ASCII, empty/null/undefined). Typecheck `pnpm tsgo:ui` exit 0; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean on touched files.

## Coordination with sibling PR #105240

Sibling PR #105240 (`fix(control-ui): preserve emoji in plugin fallback monograms`) is a separate, non-overlapping change that touches **only** `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts`. It is not affected by this PR and was left untouched. No merge conflict is expected between the two.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage: helper unit test + component test + dedicated real-browser E2E.
- Target files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`, `ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts`.
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji, joined emoji (ZWJ), flags, skin-tone variant, ASCII, empty/null, and the `Intl.Segmenter`-unavailable fallback path.
  - Surfaces: sidebar chip, agent menu row, agent selector dropdown, agents overview identity editor — all assert the intact `🚀` grapheme.

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix: allow markdown preview dialogs to scroll
target.body:
## Summary

Fix large Markdown preview dialogs being clipped instead of scrollable.

## What Problem This Solves

When a Markdown preview contains enough content to exceed the dialog height, users can only see the top part of the document. The preview body already has `overflow: auto`, but it sits inside a flex column whose ancestors do not allow the scroll area to shrink. The result is a clipped preview instead of a scrollable one.

## Fix

- Give the preview panel a viewport-bounded height.
- Set `min-height: 0` on the flex panel/body/reader path so the body can shrink and expose its scroll area.
- Preserve fullscreen and mobile viewport bounds.

target.title: fix(irc): hide tool traces from inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC users could receive internal tool-trace banners when an assistant reply was sent from the inbound message callback. A reply containing normal text plus a failed-tool trace exposed the trace, while a trace-only reply still produced an IRC message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound IRC reply path now reuses the same assistant-visible plain-text sanitizer already declared by the IRC outbound adapter, before attachment links are formatted. The change is limited to IRC reply rendering and preserves the existing reply metadata, attachment handling, and transport behavior.

## User Impact

IRC replies now contain only assistant-visible text: mixed replies keep their useful prose, and trace-only replies are not sent. Ordinary IRC assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Before and premise

On the pre-fix code, the production-handler matrix sent both the useful text and the internal trace, and also sent a trace-only reply:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts

mixed assistant text:
expected ["Done."]
received ["Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]

trace-only assistant text:
expected []
received ["⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]
```

`deliverFormattedTextWithAttachments` only formats text and attachment links; it does not sanitize assistant-visible text. The registered IRC outbound adapter already maps the same inputs to `"Done."` and an empty string through its canonical sanitizer, which is the behavior the inbound callback had bypassed.

### After: real IRC transport proof

I ran a real ngIRCd 26.1 daemon on Linux, connected two clients through the plugin's production `connectIrcClient`, and drove the exported `handleIrcInbound` handler. The temporary proof harness replaced only agent reply generation so it could deterministically produce ordinary, mixed, and trace-only payloads. Its delivery callback matched `monitorIrcProvider` and called the connected production `IrcClient.sendPrivmsg`; the IRC socket, protocol framing, send, daemon routing, and receiver were real rather than mocked.

Daemon start and proof command:

```text

  /tmp/ngircd-proof/pkg/usr/sbin/ngircd -n \
  -f /tmp/ngircd-proof/ngircd.conf

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/irc/src/inbound.live-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

The receiver observed the following messages. The 1.5-second quiet window after the trace-only case produced no third message:

```text
ordinary received: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals."]
mixed received: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals.","Done."]
trace-only received after quiet window: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals.","Done."]

✓ delivers only assistant-visible inbound replies over ngIRCd
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

The independent daemon log confirms two real registered clients and network I/O:

```text
Accepted connection 7 from "127.0.0.1:34992"
User "ocp5568298r!~ocp5568298r@127.0.0.1" registered (connection 7).
```

target.title: fix(plugins): clone registration record metadata for transactional rollback isolation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106647 — two related rollback isolation bugs in plugin transaction snapshots:

1. **Registry record sharing**: Shallow spread (`[...value]`, `{ ...value }`, `new Map(value)`) only copied container references. Registration record objects inside arrays, Maps, and objects were shared between live registry and snapshot, so metadata mutations during a failed plugin's `register()` leaked through rollback.

2. **Active record scalar/flag leakage**: The loader (`loader-runtime-candidate.ts:492-531`) creates a transaction with the PluginRecord NOT yet in the registry. During `register()`, the plugin API mutates both the registry AND the record's mutable fields — id-collection arrays AND scalar counters (`httpRoutes`, `hookCount`) AND flags (`configSchema`, `enabled`). The original `activeRecord` snapshot only captured arrays, leaving scalars and flags to leak through to `recordPluginError`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes work together:

**`cloneRegistryEntry`** — replaces flat container copies in `snapshotPluginRegistry`. Shallow-clones individual registration records while preserving opaque plugin-owned class instances (providers, services, channels, harnesses, resolvers) by reference. Detail: for plain objects, copies each own-property — Dates become `new Date(val)`, arrays become `[...val]`, other values stay by reference.

**`snapshotActiveRecord`** — now reuses `cloneRegistryEntry` on the full PluginRecord instead of only capturing arrays. This restores every transaction-owned mutable field on rollback: arrays, scalars (`httpRoutes`, `hookCount`), booleans (`configSchema`, `enabled`, `memorySlotSelected`), and Dates (`failedAt`). Runtime objects (`configUiHints`, `configJsonSchema`, `contracts`) are preserved by reference identity.

Both captures cover all three registry container shapes: arrays, Maps, and plain objects.

All three production callers (`loader-runtime-candidate.ts`, `loader-channel-runtime.ts`, `loader-cli-registry.ts`) pass `activeRecord`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Internal correctness fix ensuring rollback isolation works as documented.

## Evidence

### Regression proof: before vs after (arrays + scalars + runtime identity)

Run `node_modules/.bin/tsx _proof-regression.ts`:

```
── main (before): shallow container copies, no activeRecord ──
  registry cleared:       yes
  record.toolNames:       LEAKED
  record.httpRoutes:      LEAKED
  record.hookCount:       LEAKED
  record.configSchema:    LEAKED
  Verdict: BUG — scalars and arrays leaked through rollback

── PR (after): cloneRegistryEntry registry + full activeRecord ──
  registry cleared:       yes
  record.toolNames:       restored
  record.httpRoutes:      restored
  record.hookCount:       restored
  record.configSchema:    restored
  runtime obj identity:   preserved (===)
  Verdict: FIXED — all metadata restored, references preserved
```

### Test suite: 9/9 pass

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

New test (`"restores the active PluginRecord's arrays and scalars after a failed registration"`) mutates arrays (`toolNames`, `hookNames`, `providerIds`) AND scalars (`httpRoutes: 5`, `hookCount: 3`, `configSchema: true`, `memorySlotSelected: true`, `enabled: false`) during simulated `register()`, then verifies ALL are restored after rollback.

New test (`"preserves runtime object identity on the active PluginRecord through rollback"`) verifies `configUiHints` object reference survives rollback intact (`===`).

### Static checks: clean

- **oxlint**: zero warnings on all changed files
- **oxfmt**: clean formatting on all changed files

target.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap
target.body:
Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. The Codex review classified this as P0 / impact:security with 0.96 confidence.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MEMORY.md should not be injected as a bootstrap file in shared channel (group/channel) sessions
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/group-session-memory-privacy-108881`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace.test.ts src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts src/routing/session-key.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts --run

```

**E2E pipeline verification** — full `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` with real filesystem, covering the exact session key shapes used by Telegram groups and Discord guilds in production:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/e2e-108881-verification.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. All 9 shared channel session key types (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal + thread/legacy variants) exclude MEMORY.md from bootstrap
  2. All 5 private session key types (main, chat, direct, DM) retain MEMORY.md
  3. Hook-injected MEMORY.md is re-stripped by `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` for group sessions
  4. Hook-injected lowercase `memory.md` alias is also stripped for group sessions
  5. Subagent and cron allowlists unchanged
-  Sending a real message to a live Telegram group / Discord guild and observing the agent's response not contain private memory content. This requires running gateway + channel bot credentials which are not available in CI. The **live chain verification above** and the **canary integration tests below** prove the complete code path from `buildAgentPeerSessionKey` through `isSharedChannelSessionKey` through `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` through `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` — every production function in the critical path is exercised with real inputs and outputs.

**DM-vs-group canary integration tests** — 18 tests proving the full production session key chain (`buildAgentPeerSessionKey` → `isSharedChannelSessionKey` → `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` → `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`) with a canary workspace containing `MEMORY.md` with content `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`:

Key canary scenarios:
- **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`
- **DM non-regression**: A hook that adds `EXTRA.md` in a Telegram DM session — both `MEMORY.md` and `EXTRA.md` are preserved
- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — this restricts data access (removes MEMORY.md from shared sessions), which is the security fix

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: E2E pipeline test with real filesystem covering 38 test cases across all 7 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal); unit tests cover 21 session key shapes for `isSharedChannelSessionKey`; integration tests cover group session bootstrap file filtering and DM session preservation; hook bypass test verifies post-hook enforcement; bootstrap-extra-files hook compatibility verified for group sessions; **18 DM-vs-group canary integration tests** prove the full production session key chain with a canary `MEMORY.md` containing `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"` — confirming no group session can access the canary content while all DM sessions can
- Edge cases checked: Discord guild/channel legacy format, WhatsApp group JID, Telegram thread sub-session, Feishu nested topic/sender, undefined/null sessionKey, hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files, hook injecting lowercase `memory.md` alias, DM-vs-group asymmetry on same workspace

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — MEMORY.md was documented as private-session-only; this enforces the documented contract
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — This is the channel-agnostic, table-driven approach that the Codex review requested: "core should enforce that invariant generically across shared channel session shapes without adding configuration surface."
- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern
- **Alternative considered**: Telegram-specific predicate (rejected — would leave Discord/Slack/etc. unenforced); new config option (rejected — violates AGENTS.md "config bar is high" and Codex review "without adding configuration surface")

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis and code implementation for #108881 MEMORY.md cross-session privacy boundary

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Existing users who rely on MEMORY.md being available in group sessions (contrary to documented behavior).

**Mitigation**: The documented contract already states MEMORY.md is private-session-only. Memory remains accessible via `memory_search`/`memory_get` tools in group sessions. The `USER.md` file (stable shared instructions) is preserved in group sessions per `docs/channels/discord.md:290`.

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change — this enforces an existing documented contract that was previously unimplemented.

target.title: fix(video-generation): bound stalled video download response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseWithLimit()` in video/music generation provider download paths capped `maxBytes` but omitted `chunkTimeoutMs`. A server that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, exhausting the Gateway connection pool under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on every video/music download path that was missing them, matching `google/video-generation-provider.ts` and `anthropic/usage.ts`. Resolve `ProviderOperationTimeoutMs` (number | `() => number`) to a concrete number before passing it to `chunkTimeoutMs` so TypeScript and the idle timer see a finite budget. Add a caller-path OpenAI regression that feeds a never-chunking `ReadableStream` body and asserts the production download error within the request deadline.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled upstream video/music download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** Download body reads fail closed after the operation idle budget with a clear `…download stalled: no data received for Nms` error, releasing the connection.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/{openai,byteplus,runway,fal,together,openrouter,minimax}/video-generation-provider.ts`, `extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.ts`, `extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts`, `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `buildOpenAIVideoGenerationProvider().generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit(..., { chunkTimeoutMs, onIdleTimeout })`
- Type fix: `ProviderOperationTimeoutMs` resolved via `resolve*VideoDownloadTimeoutMs` / `resolveMinimaxRequestTimeoutMs` before `chunkTimeoutMs`

## Real behavior proof

### Caller path

`extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` `generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit` with `chunkTimeoutMs` from the request deadline resolver.

### Commands

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ openai video generation provider > times out stalled generated video download bodies via chunkTimeoutMs 82ms
✓ openai video generation provider > rejects generated video downloads that exceed the configured media cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.11s
```

Stalled body fixture: `ReadableStream` that accepts headers / opens the body but never enqueues chunks. With `timeoutMs: 80`, the production path rejects with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 80ms` in ~82–97ms (not the 120s default).

### What was not tested

Live vendor CDN stall against OpenAI/BytePlus/Runway/etc. Sibling providers share the same `readResponseWithLimit` wiring pattern; OpenAI is the exercised caller path.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the timeout resolver types, mock deadline contract, and caller-path proof output.

target.title: fix(config): fall back to provider-level contextWindow/maxTokens in model defaults
target.body:
Closes #105803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` once at the provider level would see static configured models ignore those values and fall back to global defaults unless every model repeated them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static config materialization path now uses the same precedence as the discovered-model path: per-model value, then provider-level value, then the global default. Existing output-token clamping and Mistral safety normalization remain in the canonical defaulting path.

## User Impact

Users can define shared token limits once under `models.providers.<provider>`. Explicit per-model values still win, invalid provider-level values still fall back safely, and `maxTokens` cannot exceed the effective context window.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** provider-level `contextWindow` and `maxTokens` were ignored during a real static config load.
- **Real environment tested:** secretless GitHub Actions runner, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24, patch head `4a44a1d0494cca70c293e7476490fb911c8e5849` plus a temporary proof-only workflow commit. The proof branch was deleted after the run. The current branch is a semantic-equivalent rebase onto upstream main at `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** wrote an isolated `openclaw.json`, set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `node --import tsx --input-type=module` and called `loadConfig({ pin: false, skipPluginValidation: true, skipShellEnvFallback: true })`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the successful `node` config-load run: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29501001707

```json
{
  "providerInheritanceAndClamp": {
    "contextWindow": 50000,
    "maxTokens": 50000
  },
  "perModelPrecedence": {
    "contextWindow": 32000,
    "maxTokens": 2000
  },
  "mistralSafetyNormalization": {
    "contextWindow": 262144,
    "maxTokens": 16384
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** provider-only values survive the actual config-loading path, inherited output tokens are clamped to the inherited context window, explicit model values take precedence, and Mistral's safe output cap still applies.
- **What was not tested:** a live provider API request or long-running Gateway session; this change only materializes numeric model limits and does not alter provider transport behavior.

### Regression coverage

Focused tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts` cover:

- provider-level inheritance;
- per-model precedence;
- inherited `maxTokens` clamping;
- invalid provider-level fallback;
- inherited Mistral safety normalization.

All checks on the current exact head `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4` are green: 64 successful, 35 skipped, and 1 neutral check with no failures, including `check-lint`, production/test type checks, `build-artifacts`, CodeQL config-boundary review, the Real behavior proof gate, and all selected test shards.

### Compatibility note

Existing configurations that already set provider-level values will begin honoring them for models without explicit overrides. This is the intended behavior described by the public config surface and #105803; per-model settings remain authoritative.

### Alternative considered

#105807 changes the same canonical `applyModelDefaults` boundary and additionally propagates provider-level `contextTokens`. This PR intentionally limits the compatibility change to the two fields reported and reproduced by #105803, while covering invalid provider values and inherited Mistral normalization. Maintainers can choose the broader candidate if `contextTokens` should be activated in the same release; only one implementation should land.

target.title: fix(agents): inherit materialized runtime tools
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep spawned-child tool inheritance capped to the parent's actual final tool surface when MCP/LSP tools materialize after core tools are constructed.
- Share a mutable inherited allowlist reference with embedded attempt preparation, then refresh it only after final policy filtering, runtime normalization, local-model filtering, and schema compatibility checks.
- Preserve existing unrestricted behavior and cover overlapping allow globs, policy-denied runtime tools, and schema-quarantined runtime tools.

Refs #85030

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` is constructed before bundle MCP/LSP runtimes are materialized. When a parent had a restrictive inherited tool policy, the captured child allowlist therefore contained only the earlier core tool surface and silently omitted otherwise-authorized runtime tools.

This change does not carry broad selectors such as `bundle-mcp` into child state. Instead, it refreshes the shared cap from concrete tool names on the final model-visible surface. That preserves intersections between configured and inherited globs and cannot reintroduce tools removed by later deny or schema-quarantine layers.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-construction-plan.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts --reporter=dot` (7 files, 212 tests passed)
- `pnpm format:check -- <7 changed files>`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main ...` (clean, no findings)
- `pnpm exec tsx test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/agent-bundle-mcp-tools-docker-client.ts` (real stdio MCP server, production materialization and invocation; `ok: true`)

The real stdio MCP probe materialized and invoked `dockerProbe__docker_probe`; coding and messaging profiles exposed all three probe/resource tools, while minimal and explicit deny policies exposed zero.

`corepack pnpm test:docker:cron-mcp-cleanup` also completed the current-branch OpenClaw build and package-tarball integrity check. The container phase could not start on this host because no Docker CLI is installed, so it is not reported as a passing Docker run.

## Review Notes

The first review iteration identified two selector-based risks: broad-selector deny bypass and loss of overlapping glob intersections. The implementation was replaced with concrete post-materialization allowlist refresh. A later review identified refresh before schema quarantine; the refresh now uses `schemaProjection.tools`. Fresh local and branch reviews are clean.

target.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an isolation gap where core-owned restart-recovery coordination could be exposed, overwritten, or lost through Plugin SDK session APIs.

Upstream now persists channel-turn recovery fields under the `restartRecovery*` namespace. This PR keeps those shipped fields, as well as the later split series' `mainRestartRecovery` aggregate, out of plugin reads, callback inputs, replacements, ACP resolution, and injected runtime surfaces.

The repair also addresses two earlier review findings: an identity-preserving whole-store key move could silently drop private recovery state, and the ACP SDK declared that it returned the internal `AcpSessionManager` class even though the runtime object was already a restricted facade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin-visible session rows now pass through one projection/reconciliation owner. The public `SessionEntry` type omits `mainRestartRecovery` and the complete `restartRecovery*` namespace, matching runtime behavior.

Private recovery state is retained for same-key updates and for a unique one-to-one `sessionId` key move. It is not copied when the source or destination mapping is ambiguous, and it is cleared when the effective session identity changes. Future `restartRecovery*` plugin extension slots are reserved before a new core field can collide with them.

The ACP getter returns an explicit `AcpSessionManagerFacade` interface. The runtime object remains stable, frozen, null-prototype, and limited to bound public methods, so plugins cannot reach the internal manager constructor or bypass session projection.

Compatibility note: released `v2026.7.1-beta.5` / `v2026.7.1` and the frozen PR #96230 returned the real manager class. This PR intentionally does not preserve `instanceof`, prototype, or constructor identity because exposing the internal constructor would reopen the private-session-state escape path. The SDK catalog documents that contract for maintainer review.

## User Impact

Plugin authors continue to use the same session and ACP methods, while current and future core restart-recovery coordination remains private and survives valid session-key moves.

Plugins that relied on `getAcpSessionManager()` being an actual internal class instance must migrate to the structural `AcpSessionManagerFacade` contract. No session schema, storage format, ACP method behavior, retry budget, or production `mainRestartRecovery` writer is added by this PR.

## Evidence

- Recovery isolation matrix: 9 files, 82/82 tests passed across direct Plugin SDK APIs, modern and deprecated whole-store mutation, unique and ambiguous key moves, ACP, agent runtime, channel runtime, combined transcript-store reads, injection rejection, and session identity rotation.
- Plugin SDK surface budget tests: 10/10 passed.
- Public API contract: generated declarations expose the projected `SessionEntry` and `AcpSessionManagerFacade`; no `mainRestartRecovery` or `restartRecovery*` declaration remains in the generated SDK baseline.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, public export budget, formatting, lint, max-lines ratchet, and diff-check passed after syncing to exact base `ba65a56ffd964092d1590fb1b4563ded6ed20efc`.
- Upstream's current public Plugin SDK export baseline is 7,986; this PR's reviewed `AcpSessionManagerFacade` is the sole additional export, for a passing budget of 7,987.
- Source audit found no remaining critical, major, minor, security, performance, persistence, or public-contract issue.
- Frozen PR comparison at `edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9` confirms that its whole-store implementation lacked cross-key recovery transfer and its ACP SDK returned the internal class directly.
- The branch contains zero production `mainRestartRecovery` producers. Existing upstream `restartRecovery*` writers remain unchanged and now sit behind the Plugin SDK projection boundary.

Protected local TypeScript validation could not be recorded because this machine cannot attest the required cgroup limits; the guard stopped before execution and was not bypassed. GitHub CI remains the authoritative protected typecheck/build lane.

Per maintainer-requested workflow for this split, the final audit is a complete code-diff/source review rather than a separate automated final-review pass.

target.title: fix: gateway.cmd launcher garbles non-ASCII profile paths on non-CJK Windows locales
target.body:
Closes #108774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users whose profile path contains non-ASCII characters outside the CJK range (Turkish, Cyrillic, Greek, Western European accents, ...) can install OpenClaw but the managed Gateway never starts: the generated `gateway.cmd` launcher garbles the profile path and the launch chain dies with "The system cannot find the path specified" / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

#107751 fixed this failure for CJK locales by encoding the launcher in the system ANSI code page — but only on locales where ANSI == OEM, and it deliberately left windows-125x hosts on plain UTF-8 ("ANSI bytes would just be a different flavor of wrong there"). On those hosts (e.g. Turkish: ANSI 1254, OEM 857) cmd.exe still reads the UTF-8 launcher in its OEM code page and the mojibake from #108774 persists.

## Why This Change Was Made

cmd.exe parses batch files with the **console code page**, which a fresh console (Task Scheduler, Startup folder, double-click) initializes from the boot-time registry `OEMCP` — not from the ANSI page, and not from whatever a parent session last `chcp`'d to. So the launcher encoder now targets the OEM page directly instead of approximating it via ANSI:

- `resolveWindowsOemEncoding()` (new, `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`) reads `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage\OEMCP` once (cached) through a narrow `queryWindowsRegistryValue` export that reuses the existing reg.exe query logic in `src/infra/windows-install-roots.ts`.
- `encodeWindowsLauncherScript` (`src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.ts`) encodes non-ASCII `.cmd` content to that OEM page with the same `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=<label>` marker and fail-closed round-trip verification introduced in #107751. The `CMD_ANSI_EQUALS_OEM_ENCODINGS` special case is deleted: on CJK locales OEMCP == ACP, so those hosts resolve the identical labels (gbk/big5/shift_jis/euc-kr/windows-874) and produce byte-identical launchers — no behavior change there.
- Newly covered OEM single-byte pages: 437, 720, 737, 775, 850, 852, 855, 857, 858, 860–863, 865, 866, 869 (iconv-lite `cp###` labels; iconv-lite 0.7.2 is already a root dependency since #107751).
- The decoder is untouched — the marker mechanism was already label-generic, so launchers written by any prior version still read back correctly (including legacy `gb18030`-marked files).

Design notes:

- **Why not `%APPDATA%`/`%ProgramFiles%` substitution (the issue's suggested fix):** the ClawSweeper review on #108774 correctly notes that would break custom npm prefixes, portable Node, and version managers. This fix keeps the installer-resolved paths and makes the encoding correct instead.
- **Round-trip verification decoder:** WHATWG `TextDecoder` where its tables match Windows (gbk/big5/shift_jis/windows-874 — it also flags best-fit hazards like shift_jis `¥` → 0x5C); iconv's own decode for euc-kr (Node ICU is KS X 1001-only and false-rejects cp949/UHC extension syllables) and for all `cp###` pages (no WHATWG decoder exists; WHATWG `ibm866` even disagrees with Windows CP866 at 0x1A/0x1C/0x7F). Safe because iconv-lite never best-fits — unmappable characters become `?` and fail the round-trip, aborting the install with the existing clear error.
- **Deliberate omissions, commented in the map:** CP864 (Arabic OEM) repurposes ASCII `0x25 "%"`, which generated cmd scripts contain, and the corruption would round-trip cleanly through iconv's own model — modern Arabic Windows uses OEM 720 (included) anyway. CP1258 (Vietnamese, the one locale whose OEMCP is a windows-125x page) is omitted because iconv-lite cannot round-trip Vietnamese combining forms; it keeps today's UTF-8 fallback instead of turning mojibake into a hard install error. Hosts with the "UTF-8 worldwide" beta (OEMCP 65001) keep plain UTF-8, which is correct there.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway install` + `gateway start` now works for Windows accounts with Turkish/Cyrillic/Greek/Western-European/etc. non-ASCII usernames — previously the P0 release-blocker path in #108774. CJK users see byte-identical output to #107751. ASCII-only installs are untouched (encoder still short-circuits before any code-page probe).

## Evidence

**Live before/after on a real affected host** — Windows 11 Pro, Turkish locale (registry ACP 1254 / OEMCP 857), i.e. exactly the ANSI≠OEM case #107751 left open. A launcher with `buildTaskScript`-shaped content (`cd /d`, `set "OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=..."`, node invocation) pointing into a `...\ev-yiğit-öğün\` profile directory, executed under a CP857 console (what Task Scheduler provides):

Before (bytes exactly as origin/main writes them on this host — UTF-8 fallback):

```
Sistem belirtilen yolu bulamıyor.            <- cd /d failed ("The system cannot find the path specified")
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\...\ev-yi─şit-├Â─ş├╝n\probe.js'   <- UTF-8 bytes misread as CP857
exit code: 1
```

After (bytes from the fixed `encodeWindowsLauncherScript()`, real production function + real registry read, which resolved `cp857` and emitted the `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=cp857` marker):

```
PROBE_OK cwd=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün
PROBE_OK stateDir=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün\state
exit code: 0
```

**Tests** (all pass, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...`): `src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-task-restart.test.ts` — 49 tests. New regression cases: cp857 Turkish path round-trip with marker, cp850 Western European, OEMCP-65001 stays UTF-8, unrepresentable characters on a single-byte OEM page fail the install fail-closed. All #107751 CJK cases (GBK/UTF-8 byte-collision, cp949 UHC syllables, 🚀 rejection) pass unchanged with OEM-based resolution.

`oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no errors in touched files (the 42 pre-existing errors on this machine reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout — local env, unrelated).

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## PR/Commit Surface Breakdown

Source: 29 files, +846 / -81
Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20
Total: 40 files, +2078 / -101

- Confirm Discord progress remains opt-in and best-effort.
- Review source-message id propagation and tracker keying for channel/thread isolation.

target.title: fix(e2e): bound OpenShell install script download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenShell E2E test workflow pipes the install script directly through a shell pipeline without any network deadline. A registry endpoint that accepts the connection and then stalls can hold the install step for an excessive period or concatenate partial output into shell execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The install script is now downloaded to a temporary file before execution with a 10-second connection deadline and a 120-second per-attempt deadline with two retries separated by two seconds. This prevents a stalled download from hanging the install step and ensures retries cannot concatenate partial compressed streams.

## User Impact

OpenShell E2E installs now fail within a finite window on stalled downloads instead of consuming runner time indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `bash -n .github/workflows/openclaw-live-and-e2e-checks-reusable.yml` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The workflow YAML parses with `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open("..."))'`.
- Current head is rebased onto `57ae43a89c9`.
- CI will validate the actual download and execution path.

target.title: fix(skills): support portable Copilot agent transcripts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw contributors using GitHub Copilot could not include their local Copilot sessions in agent-created PR or issue provenance. The existing helper also used POSIX-only invocation examples and did not consistently redact Windows paths, broader POSIX paths, or private local endpoints.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent transcript helper now discovers Copilot CLI sessions, keeps only visible user and assistant dialogue plus aggregate tool counts, and drops system prompts, transformed prompts, reasoning, hooks, and raw tool results. It also applies cross-platform path and private-endpoint redaction while preserving public URLs and API routes, and documents a portable `node`-based workflow.

The workflow remains local-only and fail-closed. It does not upload raw logs or add network access.

## User Impact

Developers can safely preview and optionally attach a redacted GitHub Copilot transcript when creating OpenClaw PRs or issues from Windows, macOS, or Linux. Existing Codex, Claude, Pi, and OpenClaw transcript handling remains supported.

AI-assisted: Yes. I reviewed the implementation, understand the behavior, and verified the resulting transcript output.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/agent-transcript.test.ts`
  - 4 tests passed
- `node --check .agents/skills/agent-transcript/scripts/agent-transcript`
- `oxfmt --check .agents/skills/agent-transcript/SKILL.md test/scripts/agent-transcript.test.ts`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- Real local Copilot session rendered as `copilot`, with no generated truncation marker
- Structured autoreview against `upstream/main`
  - no accepted or actionable findings

### Local cross-platform proof

- Windows (`d4b3953a811`)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/agent-transcript.test.ts`: 4 tests passed
  - helper syntax, targeted Oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed
- WSL2 Linux
  - Ubuntu 24.04, kernel `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, Node `v24.13.0`, x64
  - production helper executed directly from the mounted worktree without installing repository dependencies
  - 21 assertions passed: Copilot discovery/classification, Windows and Linux path redaction, private endpoint redaction, public URL/API-route preservation, internal-event omission, tool summaries, and no truncation
  - rendered stats: 1 user turn, 1 assistant turn, 2 tool calls, 2 raw outputs dropped, 4 redactions, 0 unsafe omissions
